passages.p1: Many farmers still use old methods to grow potatoes and corn. Agricultural corporations use advanced technology to grow cash crops such as coffee and sugarcane.
passages.p2: Corporations received a lot of money from the government and from countries such as the United States and Japan.
passages.p3: Coffee, soybeans, meat, sugar, and bioethanol are important exports. South America also has a lot of minerals, such as oil, copper, and iron ore.
passages.p4: The governments of South America worked hard to mine minerals. Their economies grew by exporting them.
passages.p5: Japan imports a lot of iron ore and copper from South America. Brazil now makes cars and airplanes.
passages.p6: Many people are worried about environmental problems, such as forest areas decreasing. After 1970, corporations cut down large areas of tropical rainforest in the Amazon Basin.
passages.p7: Traditional farmers cut down trees but protected the forests. Corporations cut down many more trees and destroyed the forests.
passages.p8: Growing the same crops on the same land makes the soil poor. Crops don’t grow well, and agriculture is hard to continue.
passages.p9: Tropical rainforests have many kinds of plants and animals, but many of them are disappearing. Once they are gone, they will never return.
passages.p10: Too much mining destroys the environment. When the minerals are gone, the mining industry will also disappear.
